name: Relational ontology

phase_0.boundary_condition: The totality of all possible connections within a closed relational set.

VINIT.justification: The state of pure possibility before any distinction or connection exists.

TANCH.justification: The boundary containing all internal morphisms and preventing external leakage.

AFWD.justification: The movement from a source to a target within a quiver structure.

AREV.justification: The contravariant mapping that returns from target to source.

CLINK.justification: The chaining of two relations to form a single mediated relation.

IMSCRIB.justification: The identity morphism where a node relates exclusively to itself.

FSPLIT.justification: A single relation splitting into distinct parallel paths of interaction.

FFUSE.justification: The reunification of parallel paths into the original unified relation.

EVALT.justification: A relation that successfully establishes a stable connection.

EVALF.justification: A relation that fails to connect or results in a null set.

ENGAGR.justification: A state where two contradictory relations exist simultaneously without collapse.

IFIX.justification: The permanent record of a relation within the system history.

phase_3.void_description: Non-existence where no nodes or edges are defined.
phase_3.true_description: A verified and active connection between two relata.
phase_3.false_description: The absence of a connection or a broken link.
phase_3.both_description: A paradox where a connection is both present and absent.

steps.domain_action: The system begins in a state of unmanifest potential without relata.
The first node establishes self-identity to become a distinct entity.
A directed morphism extends from the first node toward a potential target.
The existence of the first directed link is recorded in the system history.
The connection branches into two distinct interpretive paths.
The primary path confirms a coherent and stable relational link.
The coherent link composes with a subsequent morphism to extend the path.
The secondary path encounters a disjoint state and fails to connect.
The failed path reverses to return to the previous stable node.
The two paths reunite to restore the original unified morphism state.
The system enters a state of entanglement where both paths are held in tension.
The resulting complex relational state is permanently fixed.
The relational set closes to form a complete and bounded ontology.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The categorical logic that defines valid morphism types.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The composition of morphisms across shared nodes.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The persistent quiver structure storing all historical links.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The sequential activation of nodes within a directed path.
phase_5.alfs_store: The fundamental axioms of relational existence.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Information density required to maintain node distinctness.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A sparse set of disconnected potential relata.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A dense network of interconnected and fixed relations.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The system preserves information through exact Frobenius inversion.
